scenario: Railway historians study heritage railways that are still operational, finding a mean route length of 3.1 km (σ=0.7 km). The operational viability threshold is 2.0 km. The true mean route length across all heritage railways ever established is desired.

data.description: Observed statistics among units that cleared the survival/publication filter

question: (a) Assuming route length is normally distributed with σ=0.7 km, solve for the pre-filter true mean μ such that E[X|X>2.0]=3.1. (b) What fraction of all original units cleared the survival filter? (c) By how much does the observed (survivor) mean overstate the pre-filter true mean?

ground_truth.explanation: The heritage railways analysed only among those still running route length set is a truncated-normal sample above the 2.0 threshold. Solving E[X|X>2.0]=μ+σφ((2.0−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((2.0−μ)/σ)=3.1 gives μ≈2.98801. Only 92.1% of all original units survived; the survivor mean overstates the true mean by 0.1120 km.

naive_answer: The true mean route length is 3.1 km because that is the observed average among heritage railways analysed only among those still running.
naive_trap: Survival/publication filters truncate the distribution from below; the observed mean among survivors is a conditional expectation and systematically overstates the pre-filter population mean.
reasoning_trace: (1) Survival filter is equivalent to truncated-normal sampling above threshold=2.0. (2) Truncated mean equation: μ+σ·φ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=3.1. (3) Numerically solve with brentq → μ≈2.98801. (4) Fraction surviving: Φ̄((2.0−2.98801)/σ)≈0.92094.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 3.1,0.7,2.0
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-20*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=200)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-2.98801)<0.005
assert abs(frac-0.92094)<0.005
assert mu_sol < obs
